A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Sparks of Cooperative Reasoning: LLMs as Strategic Hanabi Agents. Their complete text, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Hanabi benchmarks, finetuning and transfer experiments, state-tracking evaluations, and analysis of collected human play logs.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds MAPPO training results and inference-token measurements.

M1.justification: The prompting scaffolds, Best-of-K, Mixture-of-Agents, SFT, and sequential Sherlock-to-Mycroft RL procedure are retained. Replacing RLVR terminology with RL using an LLM judge describes the existing reward source more accurately; it does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 2–5-player Hanabi, HanabiLogs, HanabiRewards, human play logs, Group Guessing Game, EventQA, IFBench, and AIME 2025. The added MAPPO and token analyses use existing Hanabi scenarios.

E2.justification: v3 adds an evaluated classical RL comparator, MAPPO, in Appendix H.2 and Table 5. v2 discusses specialized RL agents through prior work but has no corresponding MAPPO experiment. The existing LLM comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new MAPPO experiment trains separate agents for each player count using 64,000 games each and reports averages over 6,400-game training windows. The token analysis measures input and output tokens over 10 games per scaffold and player count. Existing benchmark protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix H.2 adds analysis of MAPPO learning dynamics and relative training-data requirements; H.3 adds inference-cost analysis across scaffolds and player counts. Existing prompting ablations, state-tracking evaluations, failed-training analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Existing fixed-seed lists, repeated-run counts, standard-deviation reporting, and IQM plots with 95% confidence intervals are unchanged. The new tables report averages without introducing additional uncertainty estimates or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds MAPPO results, including a best cross-player training-window mean of 6.39, and token measurements showing Mycroft uses 2.08 times the input and 1.31 times the output tokens of Sherlock. Existing benchmark and Table 2 scores remain unchanged. Reported gains are corrected from 138% to 388% for Mycroft, 88% to 52% against GPT-4.1, and 1.5 to 1.7 IFBench Pass@10 points. The human-percentile statement changes from 75th to 25th.

T1.justification: The Bayesian-motivated prompting, game rules, and belief-update reasoning remain unchanged. Neither version introduces formal theorems or proofs, and no substantive mathematical definitions or derivations change.

C1.justification: The abstract corrects the stated transfer gains from 11% to 11 percentage points and from 6.4% to 6.4 points, and fixes IFBench-800K to IFBench. The central benchmarking, dataset, working-memory, cross-play, and transfer contributions retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the added MAPPO comparison in light of pretrained language capabilities and limited classical-RL training budgets. It also attributes Mycroft’s higher token consumption to maintaining working memory. Most existing limitations and future-work discussion are retained after relocation.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the 160-game RL training subset and identifies the final sequentially trained checkpoint used for token measurements. Its reproducibility statement replaces deferred dataset-release wording with a direct dataset link and present availability statement. Existing prompts, hardware, and finetuning hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Yu et al. (2022) for MAPPO and Marquez (2026) when positioning online multi-agent RL as future work. It removes Su et al. (2025), previously used to justify RLVR terminology. Most other reference changes update metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: Future Work moves from Appendix A to Section 6, appendices are renumbered, and the reproducibility statement becomes part of the impact statement. Local prose, terminology, cross-references, author information, and conference front matter are edited; most narrative text is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 5–6, moves the Mycroft schematic from Figure 20 to main-text Figure 3, and relocates several existing plots. The finetuning chart becomes a clearer vector display in Figure 8a, and table formatting improves. Other plotted content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves accuracy by correcting percentage calculations and the contradictory human-quartile statement, while clearer figures, token-cost measurements, and a direct dataset link improve usability and transparency. The MAPPO addition offers limited comparative evidence because it contrasts training-window scores and different training regimes. These benefits constitute a modest improvement without changing the main scientific results.
